agent.name: Stravinsky
agent.role: Offensive security reviewer using STRIDE and OWASP methodology

findings.title: Workspace files hijack the Python version checks
findings.detail: validate-design runs python3 -c while WORKDIR is the bind-mounted /workspace. Python searches the current directory before site-packages for -c execution, so repository files named jsonschema.py or yaml.py replace the installed packages. Import-time code executes and can report the expected __version__, making the check green while running attacker code.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker adds jsonschema.py at the repository root in a pull request. CI mounts the checkout at /workspace and starts validate-design. The import executes attacker code as builder, which reads the checkout and container-visible credentials, modifies writable workspace files, and sets __version__ to 4.23.0 so validation succeeds. yaml.py provides the same path for the second check.
findings.exploitability: Remote authenticated/untrusted-PR attacker; automatic CI run; no physical access. Impact is bounded by the container's builder privileges and actual network isolation, but the checkout, cache mounts, and builder-readable environment remain available.
findings.evidence: Containerfile:311-350 sets /workspace as WORKDIR and bind-mount target; validate-design:126-127 imports unqualified jsonschema and yaml modules.

findings.title: Pip can execute an untrusted distribution as root while building the image
findings.detail: The dependency install occurs before USER builder and does not require wheels. A hash-locked source distribution can execute setup.py or a PEP 517 build backend and install hooks as UID 0. Hash verification authenticates selected bytes, not package intent, and --no-deps does not disable build-backend execution.
findings.attack_scenario: A dependency maintainer, compromised package account, or compromised dependency-update process introduces a malicious source distribution and its hash into the reviewed lock. A routine rebuild runs pip install as root; the build hook writes a backdoor into /usr/local or /opt, alters the validator, and captures build credentials or artifacts. Every consumer of the resulting image then executes the poisoned toolchain.
findings.exploitability: Remote supply-chain attacker or attacker able to land an approved lock refresh; automated image build triggers it; no physical access. The code runs with build-time root privileges and can affect the published image, while host escape still depends on the builder.
findings.evidence: PIP_ROOT_USER_ACTION=ignore at Containerfile:76-77 documents root installation; USER builder is not set until line 344; the install has no binary-only constraint.

findings.title: The build-time network allowlist is documentation only
findings.detail: The file lists an endpoint allowlist, but no RUN instruction or image-level mechanism constrains build egress. Package build code executes inside ordinary network-capable build steps and can connect outside PyPI, npm, Debian, or nodejs.org. Runtime --network=none does not protect the build phase.
findings.attack_scenario: During a rebuild, malicious Python build-backend code from the locked dependency set opens a connection to 169.254.169.254, a private 10.0.0.0/8 service, or an attacker-controlled collector. It probes internal services and sends build environment data while the build has network access, then leaves a payload in the generated image.
findings.exploitability: Remote supply-chain attacker plus an automated build on a runner with unrestricted egress; no physical access. Exploitation fails only if an external builder firewall independently supplies the missing restriction.
findings.evidence: The allowlist appears only in comments at Containerfile:36-43; pip runs in an ordinary RUN at lines 191-192.

findings.title: npm ci --ignore-scripts does not sandbox runtime dependency code
findings.detail: --ignore-scripts suppresses npm lifecycle hooks during installation, but the complete third-party tree is exposed as executable global CLI tools. Running a CLI or its version path loads JavaScript from the package and transitive dependencies. Lock integrity proves release bytes, not that a release is benign.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker compromises an npm maintainer account or gets a backdoored dependency accepted in a lock refresh. The build succeeds because install hooks are ignored. On the next CI run, validate-design executes markdownlint --version and markdown-link-check --version, or the docs job runs those CLIs over the checkout. Malicious module code runs as builder, reads /workspace and CI environment data, alters reports, and exfiltrates data when runtime networking is available.
findings.exploitability: Remote supply-chain attacker; ordinary CI startup or docs validation supplies the trigger; no physical access. The process is non-root but can access builder-readable files, environment data, and the mounted workspace.
findings.evidence: package.json:7-8 selects the CLIs; package-lock.json:1049-1067 and :1101-1124 define executable entries; validate-design:135-136 invokes them.

findings.title: Runtime network isolation is not enforced, enabling link-checker SSRF
findings.detail: The image contains a network-capable Markdown link checker and proxy/HTTP stack, but --network=none exists only in comments and an example invocation. A caller that omits the flag gives the checker normal network access. Repository-controlled Markdown links then become an SSRF and internal-network request primitive.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker adds a Markdown link to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or http://127.0.0.1:2375/containers/json. A networked docs-validate job invokes markdown-link-check; it fetches the attacker-selected endpoint and can follow an attacker-controlled redirect, probing or triggering internal services and exposing response-derived status or data through the validation report.
findings.exploitability: Remote authenticated/untrusted-PR attacker with automatic CI execution, provided the job or developer grants network access; no physical access. The image provides no enforcement when the launcher is misconfigured.
findings.evidence: package-lock.json:828-839 includes link-check and :1884-1897 includes proxy-capable clients; Containerfile:353-354 presents --network=none as caller convention.

findings.title: Unversioned apt packages drift into a privileged build and runtime image
findings.detail: The base image is digest-pinned, but ca-certificates, curl, git, and xz-utils are selected from the live Debian repository with no package version or snapshot pin. A later rebuild can silently consume a newly compromised or vulnerable signed package.
findings.attack_scenario: An upstream Debian package or signing/repository supply chain is compromised and publishes a malicious xz-utils or curl update. A scheduled rebuild accepts the newest package, and the root build executes it while extracting Node or downloading dependencies. The package poisons /opt/node, the validator, or the published image without a source change in this repository.
findings.exploitability: Remote supply-chain attacker; requires control of an upstream signed distribution path and a subsequent automated rebuild; no physical access. Normal repository signature checking does not address malicious code shipped in a trusted release.
findings.evidence: Unversioned package names are installed at Containerfile:128-134, while the comments at lines 123-127 treat the base digest as pinning the apt package set.

findings.title: The default validator is a tool-presence check, not design validation
findings.detail: The default command never opens /workspace/docs, schemas, ADRs, capability matrices, or evidence manifests. It returns success after checking tool versions only. If the CI result is used as the design-integrity gate, the named validator can be satisfied while governed design content is absent, malformed, or tampered with.
findings.attack_scenario: A pull-request author changes an architecture schema or removes required evidence. CI starts the image's default validate-design command; every installed tool reports its expected version, no design file is examined, and the command exits 0. The pipeline accepts or publishes tampered design material as if it passed validation.
findings.exploitability: Remote authenticated/untrusted-PR attacker; automatic CI is the only trigger; no physical access. Impact is conditional on this exit status being used as an authorization or release gate; the file labels the missing validation as a follow-up.
findings.evidence: validate-design:9-14 explicitly states the placeholder scope; lines 101-136 perform only version checks and lines 138-144 emit unconditional success.
